question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 17 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 21 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 19 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let total work be the LCM of 17, 21, and 19 = 6783 units.

Combined efficiency = (6783 ÷ 17) + (6783 ÷ 21) + (6783 ÷ 19) = 399 + 323 + 357 = 1079 units/hour.

Time required when working together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency.

⇒ Time = 6783 ÷ 1079 = 6 ³⁰⁹/₁₀₇₉ hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 ³⁰⁹/₁₀₇₉ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipe A = 17 hours

Time taken by pipe B = 21 hours

Time taken by pipe C = 19 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of times taken by all individual pipes.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Efficiency of pipes A, B, and C together = 399 + 323 + 357 = 1079 units/hour

⇒ Total Time taken together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time = 6783 ÷ 1079

⇒ Time = 6 ³⁰⁹/₁₀₇₉ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 6 ³⁰⁹/₁₀₇₉ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

Inlet pipes fill the tank (assigned positive efficiency), while outlet pipes empty it (assigned negative efficiency). Net efficiency is the algebraic sum of all actively working pipes.

Concept of Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. For any given setup, Work = Efficiency × Time.

Work Equivalence

If multiple independent units contribute to a shared objective, their per unit outputs (1/TA + 1/TB + 1/TC) directly sum up to equal the net output rate (1/TTₒₜₐₗ).
